title: reclaim-disk.sh tier 3 breaks the installed dependency tree
attempted: Ran ./scripts/reclaim-disk.sh to get above the eval harness's 5 GB floor.

Recommend either dropping the prune from tier 3 or having it print that a `pnpm install --recursive` is now required. Not fixed here - it is outside the CV sprint and wants its own item.

title: Family aggregation in the candidate deriver
attempted: Derived one family candidate per kind FROM the per-symbol candidates: disjunctive matcher via multi-entry required_calls (which accepted_auth_helpers_for_convention already reads as a set of alternatives, so required_calls_any_of would have been a second code path for existing semantics), coverage as the union of files any member satisfies, per-member evidence counts and join reason in requires, and superseded_by on the per-symbol members (new engine field, core schema field, migration 033, review-item surface).
evidence: 18 tests in crates/drift-engine/tests/convention_families_cv1.rs, negative controls before recall. Measured on real dub: auth 0.0324 (best per-symbol) -> 0.5709 (family) with exactly withAdmin/withPartnerProfile/withPublishableKey/withSession/withWorkspace; rate limit 0.0385 -> 0.0526 with ratelimit/ratelimitOrThrow; papermark rate limit 0.0813 with checkRateLimit/ratelimit; no family on taxonomy, formbricks, calcom, midday, openstatus. Independent verification byte-compared taxonomy's infer-candidates output against a pre-CV-1 engine on the same captured 3.2MB request: identical, and superseded_by absent rather than null.
expected_drift: Auth coverage 0.5709 is UNDER the plan's >=0.6 target. Recorded as measured rather than tuned toward the number. No request-validation family on any repo: dub has zero request_validation_called facts, so its validation candidates are name-matching with no positive evidence behind them, and aggregating them was what produced the 89-member family. papermark's candidate set changes (it gains a rate-limit family) - a second repo affected, beyond the auth story the plan describes.
diagnosis: The plan's stated rule - name-similarity nominates, resolved-module identity confirms - is INSUFFICIENT, and implementing it exactly over-aggregated on the repo the plan itself cites. Real modules export heterogeneous symbols: @/lib/auth exports the wrappers and also hashPassword, hashToken, validatePassword. Module recruitment produced a 9-member auth family holding three crypto utilities and an 89-member request-validation family holding bulkDeleteLinks and addDomainToVercel. All 10 unit tests passed on that version, because synthetic fixture modules are homogeneous. Only the dub measurement caught it. Confirmation is therefore per-kind: auth requires the call to WRAP the handler (its span strictly encloses a response/data-operation/request-input fact in the same file, in >=2 files), while rate limit and request validation recruit nothing on module identity and take only positively detected symbols.

title: Independent verification of CV-1, and the seven defects it confirmed
attempted: Verification by a separate agent instructed to falsify the commit's claims rather than confirm them, followed by fixes for everything it confirmed.
evidence: Seven CONFIRMED defects, two live on eval repos. F3 (severe): the family's helper id key was derived from a prefix, yielding rate_limit_id where security_helpers_from_requires takes helper_id with `?` in a filter_map - so the accepted rate-limit family carried zero helpers and flagged every route in scope, including compliant ones. Strictly worse than the candidate it superseded; live on dub and papermark. F1: an auth family could contain zero auth helpers, because a nominated point call could establish a module without joining the family. F2: first-non-generic-segment keying collapsed packages/api/src/auth with packages/api/src/middleware. F5: a symbol's module came from facts[0], making family formation order-dependent. F4/F9: the nominated filter and the member sort each had NO test - deleting either left 12/12 green, and deleting the filter restored the 249-member family. F7/F8: two persisted strings were false, including the rationale a reviewer reads before accepting. F10: the DoD's ledger entry did not exist. All fixed; six mutations each now red on the test that claims to catch it.
expected_drift: Three claims survived attack and are recorded as load-bearing-and-tested: the dub auth family membership (verified across all 6 repos - no non-wrapper symbol in any family on any repo), byte-identical no-change on taxonomy vs a pre-CV-1 engine, and determinism for identical input. One residual is disclosed rather than fixed, in the ledger's false_positive_behavior field: a higher-order function exported from the family's own module joins regardless of intent. The wrapper test excludes point-call utilities but cannot tell two wrappers apart by purpose. dub having no such export is luck, not design.
diagnosis: Writing the F1 regression test showed why red-checking each fix separately matters: the first version passed under its own mutation because F2's fix already separated those modules, so it was silently testing F2. Rewritten with every symbol in one module to isolate F1. Also surfaced by the verifier's own retracted finding: `cargo test --release` REBUILDS target/release/drift-engine, the binary the CLI shells out to, so a mutation battery running beside an onboarding loop produces plausible junk measurements. The documented hazard in PROTOCOL.md is debug-vs-release; this one is release-vs-release.

title: Role-conditioned scope: cron routes are not session routes
attempted: Investigated the flavor signal CV-2 assumes exists, and resolved the design question its red #4 forces. No code written - stopping before a four-piece change I could not also verify to the standard CV-1's verification round set.
evidence: CV-2's seam says 'the facts already distinguish these: route_declared + path structure and the existing file_role_detected machinery'. They do not. On dub all 117 files under **/api/cron/** and **/api/webhooks/** carry exactly one role fact, file_role_detected: api_route, plus route_declared: POST. The whole repo emits only five role values: api_route, test, config, core_module, cli_command_module. `cron_job`, `queue_worker` and `event_handler` exist in the CanonicalRole union in packages/core/src/domain.ts but nothing emits them for these files. There is no flavor signal to condition on.
diagnosis: This collides with red #4, which is the item's most important constraint: 'The flavor predicate lives in @drift/core beside conventionScopeFiles - NOT as a second glob engine in the deriver (the BB-11 lesson; one scope predicate in the product).' The deriver is Rust and needs flavor to compute per-flavor denominators; @drift/core is TypeScript. With no fact carrying flavor, the deriver would have to do its own path matching, which is exactly the second glob engine red #4 forbids. So flavor must reach the engine as DATA, not be recomputed there.
needs: The design, resolved and ready to implement in this order: (1) packages/core/src/convention-scope.ts gains the single routeFlavor(filePath) predicate beside conventionScopeFiles, reusing matchesGlob and isNextApiRoutePath rather than introducing a matcher - flavors app | cron | webhook, defaulting to app so a repo with no cron paths yields one unconditioned family (CV-2's red #2). (2) conventionScopeFiles honours matcher.applies_to.route_flavors so enforcement narrows by flavor, mirroring the applies_to_file_roles shape required_change_checks already uses at run-check.ts:1740. (3) The infer-candidates request gains per-file flavors computed TS-side, following the existing diff_changed_files precedent in packages/cli/src/engine/engine-candidates.ts - the engine reads flavor as a field and does zero path matching, which satisfies red #4 exactly. (4) candidate_command.rs computes per-flavor denominators and emits applies_to.route_flavors on the family matcher. Then CV-2's reds: two scoped families where cron uses signature auth and session routes use wrappers; one unconditioned family where there is no flavor signal; and on dub, no cron route flagged by the session family.
expected_drift: CV-2's red #3 target - 'combined union accounts for >= 90% of the 341 measured wrapper users' - should be checked against CV-1's measured reality rather than the plan's numbers. CV-1 measured the auth family at 0.5709 coverage over 494 scope files with 372 supporting examples, and dub has 117 cron/webhook routes. Whether splitting by flavor raises or lowers per-flavor coverage is a measurement to take, not a number to assume: verifyQstashSignature was never nominated as an auth candidate at all in the CV-1 run, so the signature family CV-2 predicts may not form without work on its own nomination.

title: Role-conditioned scope: cron routes are not session routes
attempted: Flavour emitted as a route_flavor_detected fact at scan time (Geoffrey's amendment a); the deriver reads it rather than matching globs. routeFlavor added to @drift/core beside conventionScopeFiles as the single TS-side predicate; conventionScopeFiles honours matcher.applies_to_route_flavors. Per-flavour denominators and one family per flavour that has members.
evidence: dub auth family 0.5709 over 494 files -> 0.7731 over 357, same five wrappers. Flavour distribution measured: 357 api_route, 112 cron_job, 25 webhook_handler. 10 tests in route_flavor_differential_cv2.rs + 11 in packages/core/test/route-flavor-cv2.test.ts. Four mutations each red on the test that claims to catch it. eval:external 7/7 no change.

Two implementations of the flavour rule exist by necessity (engine at fact time, core for scope) and cannot share code across the process boundary; the seam is a shared table plus a test that READS the TypeScript test file and fails if a pinned path is missing from it.

title: Promotion path: presence-only enforcement beside the proof path (option B)
attempted: Geoffrey chose option B and set three binding conditions. Presence mode dispatches on matcher.enforcement_semantics == 'presence'; promotion is per candidate via isPromotedPresenceConvention, so family candidates are visible by default while the per-symbol dominance candidates of the same kinds stay quarantined.
evidence: 13 tests in presence_enforcement_cv3.rs, 7 in presence-promotion-cv3.test.ts. Condition 1: message forbids unprotected/missing auth/dominate/protected route, and states what it did not check. Condition 2: warn suggested, block only by explicit --mode block. Condition 3: guard-called-after-sink pinned as a documented non-catch, verified meaningful (red under the inverted-satisfied mutation). Four mutations bite. Full battery clean: external 7/7, determinism 7/7, evasion 91 cells, bench 0/56, beta:proof verified.
diagnosis: Two bugs found while building: route_flavor_detected was missing from the check path's inbound fact-kind parser, so every flavour-conditioned family would have silently fallen back to covering all flavours; and the presence path's own scope check re-globbed, hitting an F3 residue. Independent verification then found three more, all fixed: file-granular enforcement passed a route.ts whose GET was wrapped and whose POST wrote to the database (now per handler); namespace imports produced a FALSE POSITIVE on a default-visible convention because resolution never consulted the call fact's receiver, using a resolver this crate already had in security_patterns.rs; and the engine trusted the CLI to have applied path globs with nothing pinning it (now pinned end to end).

title: F3's shape is still live in the engine's phase5 glob matcher
attempted: Traced why the first end-to-end presence-enforcement run returned zero findings on a fixture repo where every route was a violation.
evidence: check_command.rs path_glob_matches strips the suffix /**/route.ts and then does file_path.starts_with(prefix) on the remaining literal '**/app/api'. So `**/app/api/**/route.ts` cannot match `app/api/x/route.ts`. Root-level app/api - the default create-next-app layout - matches nothing. Verified by reading the function and by the zero-finding run.
expected_drift: This is F3's exact class in a matcher F3's fix never reached, and it affects the quarantined phase5 proof paths (auth, request validation, phase6 guards) which all call phase5_file_scope_matches. Those paths are behind --experimental-security so the blast radius is bounded today, but it means the existing auth PROOF path silently does nothing on that layout. The CV-3 presence path was fixed by removing globbing from it entirely (the CLI already applies core's predicate and passes only in-scope facts). The phase5 paths are NOT changed here - they are quarantined and out of CV-3's scope. Wants its own item.
